mainTopic: Explaining 'הכל שוחטין' and 'וכולן ששחטו': רבינא's readings, why each אמורא rejected the others, and the שחיטה of a כותי
overview: The גמרא finishes testing רב אשי's reading of the opening משנה of חולין. In that reading, 'הכל שוחטין' includes a ישראל משומד whose knife is checked for him, while a חרש, שוטה, or קטן can never slaughter. The משנה's next line, 'וכולן ששחטו ואחרים רואין אותן', fits no case in this reading, so the גמרא calls it a קשיא. רבינא then offers a new reading in two versions. In the first, 'הכל' means experts in the laws of שחיטה. In the second, it means people established not to faint. In both versions, 'וכולן' refers to someone who cannot be tested or asked afterward, so only the fact that others watched him makes his שחיטה valid. The גמרא then sums up why each אמורא (אביי, רבא, רב אשי, רבה בר עולא, רבינא) did not accept the others' explanations. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that a כותי's שחיטה is permitted when a Jew watches him, or if he eats a כזית of the meat himself. It then begins a similar case that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How a careless Jew's slaughter can be permitted
steps.stepSummary: This continues the current reading of the משנה. A ישראל משומד may slaughter if someone checks his knife beforehand. If no one checked it, he should not slaughter. If he already did, the knife is checked afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone checks a knife and gives it to him, and his slaughtered meat may be eaten. If no one checked the knife and gave it to him, he should not slaughter. If he did slaughter, his knife is checked afterward. If the knife is found smooth, his meat may be eaten. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב אשי's explanation of how a משומד, a Jew who is not careful about kashrus, fits into 'הכל שוחטין' (everyone may slaughter).
steps.deeperAnalysis: We trust him to slaughter properly, but not to check that his knife has no nicks, since checking takes extra effort he may skip. So the knife is checked for him, either before (לכתחילה) or after (בדיעבד). Only if the knife was nicked is the meat forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jew who is not careful about מצוות; here, one who eats non-kosher meat for convenience
Checks the knife to make sure it has no nicks
A smooth knife with no nicks, fit for שחיטה
From the start; the proper way to act before doing something
After the fact; once it has already been done

steps.confusionAlert: Who is 'him' (לו)? It is the ישראל משומד from the lines just before this, not the חרש, שוטה, or קטן mentioned next.

phrases.english: One checks a knife and gives it to him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the Jew who eats non-kosher meat for convenience, from the lines just before this.

phrases.english: and it is permitted to eat from his slaughter.
But if one did not check it and give it to him –
he should not slaughter,
and if he did slaughter – one checks his knife afterward.
If his knife is found to be smooth –
it is permitted to eat from his slaughter,
and if not – it is forbidden to eat from his slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of 'הכל שוחטין' that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A משומד's slaughter is valid if his knife is checked, before or after; without a checked knife he should not slaughter in the first place.

steps.title: Why a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor are excluded even after the fact
steps.stepSummary: Under this reading, the משנה's words 'חוץ מחרש שוטה וקטן' mean these three can never slaughter, even בדיעבד. The worry is that they may make one of the mistakes that ruin a שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, whose slaughter is not valid even after the fact. We worry they may pause, press the knife down, or hide the knife inside the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'except' clause of the משנה within the current reading: these three are disqualified completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a משומד, the only worry is the knife, and checking it solves the problem. With a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, the worry is about how they perform the cut itself, and a later knife check cannot fix that. That is why even בדיעבד their slaughter is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor; people not held responsible for their actions
Pausing in the middle of the cut, which ruins the שחיטה
Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it back and forth
Hiding the knife under the skin or the pipes while cutting

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the problem in the next step. If these three can never slaughter, then the משנה's next line, which allows slaughter when others watch, becomes hard to place.

phrases.english: Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
for whom even after the fact it is also not valid,
lest they pause, lest they press,
phrases.notes: These are mistakes that make a שחיטה not kosher: stopping in the middle, and pushing the knife down instead of drawing it.

phrases.english: and lest they hide the knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same reading, now explaining the 'except' clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש, שוטה, or קטן cannot slaughter even בדיעבד, because they may pause, press, or hide the knife.

steps.title: What does 'and all of them who slaughtered' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case the משנה's next line, 'וכולן ששחטו,' is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'all of them who slaughtered': which case is that about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the current reading against the next line of the משנה. This question sets up the attempts to answer it that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when 'all of them' slaughter while others watch, their slaughter is kosher. Under the current reading, it is not clear which group 'all of them' could mean. The גמרא will try each option in turn.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And all of them who slaughtered,' the next line of the משנה
To which one? Which case does this refer to?

phrases.english: And 'all of them who slaughtered' –
to which case does it refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the reading from steps 1 and 2 against the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case in the משנה does 'וכולן ששחטו' refer to under the current reading?

steps.title: It cannot refer to the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor
steps.stepSummary: The first option, that 'וכולן' refers to the חרש, שוטה, and קטן mentioned right before it, is rejected because of the wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor, since that clause is right next to it, then the משנה should have said 'and if they slaughtered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the most natural answer, the case right next to the line, and pushes it away because the word 'כולן' does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כולן' (all of them) points back to the whole broad group of 'הכל,' everyone. If the משנה meant only the three people just mentioned, it would have said 'ואם שחטו.' The גמרא's objection here is only about this wording.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would say; introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test
It stands on it; it is right next to that clause
He should have said; the wording ought to have been different

phrases.english: If you say it refers to the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor –
since it stands right next to that,
it should have said 'and if they slaughtered'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the suggestion that 'וכולן' refers to the חרש, שוטה, and קטן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'כולן' does not fit a small group just mentioned; the משנה would have said 'ואם שחטו.'

steps.title: It cannot refer to a careless Jew whose knife was checked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'וכולן' refers to the ישראל משומד. If someone checked his knife beforehand, however, he may already slaughter לכתחילה, so watching him adds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to the careless Jew? If someone checked the knife and gave it to him, didn't you say he may slaughter from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, the משומד, and rejects the first version of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's line is about people whose slaughter is kosher only because others watched. A משומד with a pre-checked knife needs no one watching; step 1 already allowed him to slaughter לכתחילה. So the line cannot be about him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new suggestion after the previous one failed
But you said; points back to an earlier statement that contradicts the suggestion

phrases.english: Rather, does it refer to the careless Jew?
If it is where one checked a knife and gave it to him,
but you said he may slaughter from the start!
phrases.notes: Pointing back to step 1: with a checked knife, he slaughters even without anyone watching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4 rejected the first option, this tries the משומד and rejects the case where the knife was checked.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the משומד case only where the knife was checked beforehand.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case he may already slaughter לכתחילה, so 'others watching' is not needed.

steps.title: It also cannot refer to a careless Jew whose knife was not checked
steps.stepSummary: Suppose no one checked the knife. If the knife is still there, just check it now. If the knife is gone, watching him does not help, because watching cannot show whether the knife had a nick.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where one did not check. If the knife is here, let him check it now. If the knife is not here, what good is it that others watched him? Maybe he slaughtered with a nicked knife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last version of the משומד case and shows that 'others watching' is either unnecessary or useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a משומד, the only problem is the knife. If the knife is available, checking it solves everything, so watching is not needed. If the knife is gone, watching cannot reveal a nick, so watching does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: It is here; it is available
It is not here; it is not available
What of it? What difference does it make?
A nicked knife, which makes a שחיטה not kosher

phrases.english: Rather, it is where one did not check.
If the knife is available –
let him check it now,
and if the knife is not available –

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲחֵרִים רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: when others watch him, what of it?
Perhaps he slaughtered with a nicked knife!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off the last remaining version of the משומד option.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the משומד case where the knife was not checked, whether or not the knife is still available.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Watching is unnecessary when the knife can be checked, and useless when it cannot, since watching cannot detect a nick.

steps.title: The current reading is left with a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: No case fits 'וכולן ששחטו' under the current reading, so the גמרא declares it a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the current reading of the משנה cannot explain the line 'וכולן ששחטו.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every possible case has been ruled out: the חרש-שוטה-קטן case and both versions of the משומד case. The word 'קשיא' means the problem stands without an answer. This makes room for a new reading of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a question left unanswered, though not a final disproof like תיובתא

steps.whatToRemember: Under the reading that 'הכל שוחטין' includes a משומד, the line 'וכולן ששחטו ואחרים רואין אותן' has no case to fit. This open problem leads to רבינא's new reading.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is not the same as 'תיובתא.' It marks a serious difficulty left standing, not a complete refutation of the view.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the failure of steps 4 to 6 to answer the question of step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reading that 'הכל שוחטין' includes a משומד cannot explain 'וכולן ששחטו'; the difficulty stands.

steps.title: רבינא's new reading: everyone who is an expert may slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reads 'הכל שוחטין' differently: it means all experts may slaughter, even if they are not yet established as reliable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This is what the משנה is teaching. 'Everyone slaughters' means all experts slaughter, experts even though they are not established.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a fresh way to read the start of the משנה, so that the whole משנה makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the old reading, 'הכל' meant all kinds of people, even a משומד. רבינא says 'הכל' means everyone who is an expert, meaning someone who knows the laws of שחיטה, even if he is not known to have a steady hand that won't faint during the cut. This gives the later lines of the משנה, such as 'וכולן ששחטו,' room to talk about other kinds of people.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is teaching; introduces a new reading of the text
Experts; people who know the laws of שחיטה
Established; known from experience to be reliable

steps.whyThisMatters: This new reading replaces the one that ended in 'קשיא' and becomes the starting point for explaining the rest of the משנה.

phrases.english: Ravina said: This is what it is teaching –
'Everyone slaughters,'
meaning all experts slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: מוּמְחִין וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מוּחְזָקִין.
phrases.english: experts, even though they are not established.
phrases.notes: He means they know the laws, but we haven't yet seen that they slaughter steadily without fainting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 7 by offering a completely new reading of 'הכל שוחטין.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הכל שוחטין' includes even a ישראל משומד whose knife is checked.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הכל שוחטין' means all experts in the laws of שחיטה, even if they are not established as reliable.

steps.title: When an expert may slaughter, and testing someone after the fact
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבינא's reading: the permission applies when we know the person knows the הלכות שחיטה. If we don't know, he should not slaughter, but if he did, we test him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When we know he can say the laws of slaughtering. If we don't know that, he should not slaughter. If he did slaughter, we test him. If he knows the laws, we may eat his meat. If not, we may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the משנה the way רבינא explained it, adding a limit: the person must be known to know the הלכות שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. Before slaughtering (לכתחילה), we need to already know he knows the laws. After he slaughtered (דיעבד), we can test him, and his שחיטה depends on whether he passes.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case does this rule apply? It introduces a limit on the rule
The laws of ritual slaughtering
We test him, to see if he knows the laws
Before the act / after the fact

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
Where people know about him that he knows
how to say the laws of slaughtering.
But if people do not know about him
that he knows how to say the laws of slaughtering,
he should not slaughter.
And if he slaughtered, we test him:
if he knows how to say the laws of slaughtering,
it is permitted to eat from his slaughtering,
and if not,
it is forbidden to eat from his slaughtering.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? שֶׁיּוֹדְעִין בּוֹ שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לוֹמַר הִלְכוֹת שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבינא's reconstruction of the משנה from step 8.
steps.terutzMaskana: Knowledge of the laws must be known לכתחילה. After the fact, testing him is enough.

steps.title: Deaf-mute, mentally incompetent person and minor are excluded even after the fact
steps.stepSummary: Still in רבינא's reading: חרש, שוטה and קטן cannot slaughter even בדיעבד, because they might make a שהייה, דרסה or חלדה mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person and a minor. Their slaughtering is not valid even after the fact, because they might pause, press down, or hide the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The reading continues and excludes three types of people whose שחיטה does not work even after it was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a regular person whose knowledge was unknown, testing his knowledge of the laws afterward is enough. For these three, the worry is not what they know but how they actually performed the cut. So even after the fact we worry they paused, pressed, or hid the knife.

keyTerms.meaning: Deaf-mute, mentally incompetent person, and minor
Pausing in the middle of slaughtering, which makes it invalid
Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it back and forth
Hiding the knife under the skin or the windpipe while cutting

phrases.english: Except for a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor,
where even after the fact, it is also not valid,
lest they pause,
lest they press down,
and lest they hide the knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, דַּאֲפִילּוּ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the exception to the rule in step 9.
steps.terutzMaskana: חרש, שוטה and קטן are invalid even בדיעבד, out of fear of שהייה, דרסה and חלדה.

steps.title: Which case does 'and all of them who slaughtered' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: Under רבינא's reading, the גמרא asks again what 'וכולן ששחטו' is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And all of them who slaughtered': which case is this about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking which case in the משנה the phrase 'וכולן ששחטו' refers to under רבינא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if others watched them, their שחיטה is valid. The גמרא needs a case where watching actually helps.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of them who slaughtered (while others watched them)
On which one? Which case does it refer to?

phrases.english: "And all of them who slaughtered": on which case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבינא's reading against the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case 'וכולן ששחטו' refers to under רבינא's reading.

steps.title: It cannot refer to the deaf-mute, incompetent and minor
steps.stepSummary: If it meant חרש שוטה וקטן, the closest case, the משנה should have said 'ואם שחטו' instead of 'וכולן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about the deaf-mute, mentally incompetent person and minor, since that comes right before it, it should have said 'and if they slaughtered'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first option because of the wording, just as it did before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכולן' (all of them) sounds like a wider group. A clause going right back to the case just mentioned would say 'ואם שחטו'.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say. It introduces a possible answer
It stands on it, meaning it is right next to that case
It should have said

phrases.english: If you say it is on the deaf-mute, mentally incompetent person, and minor,
since it stands right next to it,
it should have said "and if they slaughtered"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אַחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן עֲלַהּ קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects the first answer to step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that וכולן refers to חרש שוטה וקטן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording 'וכולן' doesn't fit. It should have said 'ואם שחטו'.

steps.title: Maybe it refers to non-experts, but testing would be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'וכולן' refers to the non-experts, then objects: for them, testing after the fact is enough, so why watch them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about those who are not experts. But for them, 'we test him' is enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second option, that 'וכולן' means the non-experts, and right away pushes back on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 already said a non-expert who slaughtered is tested afterward. If testing settles it, being watched adds nothing. So this reading seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who are not experts, not known to know the laws
It is enough

phrases.english: Rather, it is on those who are not experts;
"we test him" is enough!
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to the rule from step 9: if he slaughtered, we test him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אַשֶּׁאֵין מוּמְחִין, בְּבוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ סַגִּי!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a second answer to step 11 and challenges it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Testing him afterward already solves the problem, so watching seems useless.

steps.title: Watching helps when he is not around to be tested
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: 'וכולן' refers to a non-expert who is no longer here, so we cannot test him. Then having watched him is what makes it valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he is not in front of us so that we could test him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the non-expert reading by finding a case where testing is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testing works only if the person is available. If he left, the only way to know the שחיטה was done right is that others watched him. So 'וכולן ששחטו ואחרים רואין אותן' now has a real job.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not in front of us, not available
That we could test him

steps.whatToRemember: In רבינא's first reading, 'וכולן ששחטו' refers to a non-expert who can no longer be tested. Watching him replaces the test.

phrases.english: Where he is not before us so that we could test him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Testing a non-expert always works, so watching him is useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the שוחט is gone and cannot be tested, watching him is what validates the שחיטה.

steps.title: Second version: everyone established may slaughter, even non-experts
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבינא differently: 'הכל שוחטין' means everyone who is מוחזק may slaughter, even if he is not a מומחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבינא said: this is what the משנה means by 'All may slaughter': all who are established may slaughter. Established, even though they are not experts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רבינא's explanation of 'הכל שוחטין'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the main requirement is being מוחזק, which here means known to have a steady hand and not to faint. Being a מומחה in the laws is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: Established, here meaning known not to faint while slaughtering
Experts, known to know the laws
This is what it is teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first, the key is being an expert in the laws. In this one, the key is being established not to faint, even without being an expert.

phrases.english: And there are those who say: רבינא said:
This is what it teaches: "All may slaughter":
all who are established may slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: מוּחְזָקִין אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מוּמְחִין.
phrases.english: established, even though they are not experts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, רָבִינָא אָמַר: הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבינא's reading from step 8.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הכל שוחטין' means all who are established, even if they are not experts.

steps.title: Established means he slaughtered before us without fainting
steps.stepSummary: Being מוחזק means he slaughtered in front of us two or three times without fainting. Otherwise he should not slaughter, in case he faints.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When they slaughtered in front of us two or three times and he did not faint. If he did not slaughter in front of us two or three times, he should not slaughter, because he might faint.
steps.whatsHappening: Within the second version, the גמרא explains what counts as 'established' and what happens if someone isn't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that he faints in the middle and the שחיטה becomes invalid. Slaughtering two or three times in front of us without fainting proves he is steady. Without that proof, he should not slaughter לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two or three times
He fainted
Lest he faint

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
Where they slaughtered in front of us
two or three times
and he did not faint.
But if he did not slaughter in front of us
two or three times,
he should not slaughter, lest he faint.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ לְפָנֵינוּ שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines 'מוחזקין' from step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: מוחזק means he slaughtered two or three times in front of us without fainting. Otherwise he does not slaughter לכתחילה.

steps.title: After the fact, his word that he did not faint is enough
steps.stepSummary: If someone not yet established slaughtered and says he is sure he did not faint, his שחיטה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he slaughtered and said, 'I am sure I did not faint,' his slaughtering is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The second version ends with the after-the-fact rule: we trust the שוחט's own statement that he did not faint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the pattern in the first version. לכתחילה we need proof ahead of time. בדיעבד a simple check is enough, and here the check is his own clear statement.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear to me, I am certain
His slaughtering is valid

steps.whatToRemember: Second version of רבינא: anyone established not to faint may slaughter even without being an expert. Someone not established should not slaughter, but if he did and is sure he didn't faint, it is valid.

phrases.english: And if he slaughtered and said:
"It is clear to me that I did not faint,"
his slaughtering is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם שָׁחַט וְאָמַר: ״בָּרִי לִי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְעַלַּפְתִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the בדיעבד rule for the case in step 16.
steps.terutzMaskana: בדיעבד, his certainty that he did not faint makes the שחיטה valid.

steps.title: Deaf-mute, imbecile and minor are excluded even after the fact
steps.stepSummary: In רבינא's second reading, the משנה's exception of חרש, שוטה and קטן means their שחיטה is invalid even after the fact, since they may make one of the mistakes that ruin a שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן: for them, even after the fact it is not valid. This is because they might pause, might press down, or might hide the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with רבינא's second reading of the משנה. It now explains the משנה's exception of חרש, שוטה and קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary people who are not yet מוחזק can be trusted after the fact if they say 'ברי לי'. A חרש, שוטה and קטן cannot be trusted that way at all. They might make a mistake that ruins the שחיטה (pausing, pressing, or hiding the knife), so their שחיטה is invalid even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally unfit person, and a minor: people not considered responsible for their actions
After the fact; once it has already been done
Pausing in the middle of the שחיטה, which makes it invalid
Pressing the knife down instead of moving it back and forth, which makes it invalid
Hiding the knife under the skin or the pipes while cutting, which makes it invalid

phrases.english: except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
for whom even after the fact it is also not valid,
lest they pause, lest they press,
and lest they hide the knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן דַּאֲפִילּוּ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבינא's second reading by explaining the משנה's exception clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה's clauses in a new way
steps.terutzMaskana: חרש, שוטה and קטן are invalid even after the fact, because they may pause, press or hide the knife.

steps.title: Which case does 'and all of them who slaughtered' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: Using this reading, the גמרא asks which group the משנה's words 'וכולן ששחטו' refer to.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And all of them who slaughtered': which case is this about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a test of רבינא's reading. It asks which group the משנה's next clause, 'וכולן ששחטו', is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה goes on to say that 'all of them' who slaughtered while others watched have a valid שחיטה. In this reading, we need to figure out who 'all of them' are. The next steps try out the possible answers.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of them: the משנה's word that opens the next clause
To which one? Which case is this about?

phrases.english: 'And all of them who slaughtered': to which case does it refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks how the next clause of the משנה fits the reading just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which group of people the clause 'וכולן ששחטו' is about.

steps.title: It cannot refer to the deaf-mute, imbecile and minor
steps.stepSummary: If 'וכולן' were about חרש, שוטה and קטן, the משנה should have said 'ואם שחטו', not 'וכולן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to the deaf-mute, imbecile and minor, since it stands right next to them, then it should have said 'And if they slaughtered'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, that 'וכולן' means חרש, שוטה and קטן. It rejects it based on the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חרש, שוטה and קטן are the group mentioned right before this clause. If the משנה meant only them, the simple words 'ואם שחטו' would be enough. The word 'וכולן' (all of them) sounds like it means a different or wider group.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands on it: the clause is placed right next to that case
It should have said

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא אַחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן עֲלַהּ קָאֵי,
phrases.english: If you say it refers to a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor, since it stands next to them,
it should have said 'And if they slaughtered'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אַחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן עֲלַהּ קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the first answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'וכולן' as being about חרש, שוטה and קטן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording 'וכולן' does not fit a clause about the group mentioned right before it; 'ואם שחטו' would be the natural wording.

steps.title: Maybe it means the non-established, but 'ברי לי' is enough for them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'וכולן' is about people who are not מוחזק. It objects that for them, saying 'ברי לי' already makes the שחיטה valid, so why would anyone need to watch?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to those who are not established. But didn't you say that 'It is clear to me' is enough?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second option and right away challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said that a non-מוחזק who says 'ברי לי שלא נתעלפתי' has a valid שחיטה. If his own word is enough, the משנה's requirement that others watch him seems unnecessary. So this option also looks like it fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Those not yet established as reliable slaughterers
It is clear to me: the slaughterer's own claim that he did not faint
It is enough

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to those who are not established,
but didn't you say that 'It is clear to me' is enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַשֶּׁאֵין מוּחְזָקִין וְהָאָמְרַתְּ בְּבָרִי לִי סַגִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the second option and challenges it, the same way as steps 13 and 14 did for רבינא's first reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Challenges reading 'וכולן' as being about the non-מוחזק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His own statement 'ברי לי' already makes the שחיטה valid, so watching him seems unnecessary.

steps.title: He is not here to be asked
steps.stepSummary: Watching is needed when the non-established slaughterer is not present, so we cannot ask him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is when he is not before us, so that we could ask him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. 'וכולן' is about a non-מוחזק who cannot be asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ברי לי' only helps if the slaughterer is here to say it. If he has left, the only way to know the שחיטה was done properly is that others watched him. So the משנה's rule about watching still has a purpose, and רבינא's reading holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not here
Before us
That we could ask him

steps.whatToRemember: In רבינא's second reading: a מוחזק may slaughter from the start; a non-מוחזק is valid after the fact if he says 'ברי לי', or, if he is not here, if others watched him; חרש, שוטה and קטן are invalid even after the fact.

phrases.english: Where he is not before us, so that we could ask him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Watching seems pointless, since 'ברי לי' is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Watching matters when the slaughterer is gone and cannot be asked.

steps.title: Why רבינא and רבה בר עולא rejected the other explanations
steps.stepSummary: רבינא and רבה בר עולא did not explain the משנה like אביי, רבא and רב אשי, because the word 'וכולן' did not fit those explanations well for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא and רבה בר עולא did not explain it like אביי, רבא and רב אשי, because 'וכולן' was difficult for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now sums up the whole discussion. It explains why some אמוראים chose a different explanation of the משנה than others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא on this daf explained the משנה in his own way. רבינא and רבה בר עולא felt that in the explanations of אביי, רבא and רב אשי, the word 'וכולן' did not sit well. So they built their own readings instead.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not say: they did not explain it that way
It was difficult for them

phrases.english: Ravina and Rabba bar Ulla

phrases.aramaic: כְּאַבַּיֵּי וְרָבָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי לָא אָמְרִי,
phrases.english: did not explain it like Abaye, Rava and Rav Ashi,
because 'And all of them' was difficult for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא וְרַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא כְּאַבַּיֵּי וְרָבָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי לָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from רבינא's reading to explain why the different explanations exist.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The word 'וכולן' is what pushed רבינא and רבה בר עולא away from the explanations of אביי, רבא and רב אשי.

steps.title: Why the others rejected רבה בר עולא's explanation
steps.stepSummary: The other אמוראים did not follow רבה בר עולא, who read the משנה as being about a טמא who slaughters קדשים. In their view, the main place for that law is the משנה in זבחים, which deals with קדשים, not our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them did not explain it like רבה בר עולא. According to the version where you said 'here is the main place', on the contrary: 'there' is the main place, since it deals with קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its summary. It explains why every other אמורא turned down רבה בר עולא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, one version claimed that our משנה is the main source for the law of a טמא slaughtering קדשים. The others push back: that law belongs mainly in the משנה in זבחים, which is all about קדשים. So it is unlikely that our משנה is coming to teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: Version; one way the discussion was reported
The main place where a law is taught
On the contrary
Animals set aside as offerings

steps.whatToRemember: Each explanation of 'הכל שוחטין' was rejected by others for a specific reason: 'וכולן' was hard for the explanations of אביי, רבא and רב אשי, and the 'main source' problem was hard for רבה בר עולא's.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּהוּ כְּרַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא לָא אָמְרִי,
phrases.english: All of them did not explain it like Rabba bar Ulla,
according to that version where you said 'here' is the main place:
on the contrary, 'there' is the main place,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the משנה in מסכת זבחים that also teaches about a טמא who slaughtered.

phrases.english: since it is dealing with קדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלְּהוּ כְּרַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא לָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the summary by giving the reason the others rejected רבה בר עולא's explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The others rejected רבה בר עולא's reading because the main source for a טמא slaughtering קדשים is the משנה in זבחים, not our משנה.

steps.title: Why the others reject the second version of רבה בר עולא
steps.stepSummary: Under the version where the משנה in זבחים is the main source and our משנה mentions טמא במוקדשין only because it mentioned טמא בחולין, the others object: the case of טמא בחולין was never needed at all, because חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש are not like קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the version that says the main source is there, and here the משנה taught an impure person with sacred animals only because it taught an impure person with non-sacred food: the case of the impure person with non-sacred food was not needed in the first place, because non-sacred food prepared in purity like sacred food is not treated like sacred food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other אמוראים also reject the second version of רבה בר עולא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That version says טמא במוקדשין was only added because of its 'partner' case, טמא בחולין. But the others hold that טמא בחולין is not a case worth teaching, since חולין prepared על טהרת הקודש do not have the status of קודש. So there is no 'partner' case to explain why טמא במוקדשין was added.

keyTerms.meaning: Version (of a statement)
Since he taught (this case, he also taught the other)
Non-sacred food handled with the purity rules of sacred food
Sacred animals (קדשים)

phrases.english: According to that version that you said:
there is the main place,
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה in זבחים, the one mentioned in the previous step.

phrases.english: and here, since he taught an impure person with non-sacred food,
he also taught an impure person with sacred animals –
the impure person with non-sacred food itself
was not needed for him,
non-sacred food prepared with the purity of sacred food
is not like sacred food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 24, now rejecting the second version of רבה בר עולא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The others reject this version because טמא בחולין is not a case worth teaching, so it cannot be the reason טמא במוקדשין was included.

steps.title: Why the others reject the first version of רבינא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's first version says experts may slaughter, but those not known as experts may not. The others reject this because most people who deal with slaughter are experts.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them did not explain it like רבינא. According to the version that says: experts, yes; those who are not experts, no. They hold that most people who are found around slaughter are experts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why all the other אמוראים did not explain the משנה like רבינא, starting with his first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's first version needs a difference between known experts and people not known as experts. The others say we can rely on the רוב: most people who handle שחיטה know how to do it. So a person not known as an expert is treated like an expert, and רבינא's split does not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: Experts (who know the laws of slaughter)
Majority; we follow what is usually true
People commonly involved in slaughter

phrases.english: All of them did not say like רבינא,
according to that version that says:
experts, yes,
those who are not experts, no –
most of those found around slaughter
are experts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבה בר עולא to the other side of step 23: why the others reject רבינא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since most people who handle slaughter are experts, there is no need to split between known experts and others.

steps.title: Why the others reject the second version of רבינא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's second version says people established as not fainting may slaughter, and others may not. The others reject this because we do not worry that someone will faint.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the version that says: established ones, yes; those not established, no. We are not concerned about fainting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason the others reject רבינא's second version too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version divides people into those known not to faint during slaughter and those not known. The others say fainting is not a real worry, so there is no reason to forbid someone who is not established. Without that worry, the split falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Established (known not to faint while slaughtering)
Fainting
We are not concerned

phrases.english: According to that version that says:
established ones, yes,
those not established, no –
we are not concerned about fainting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 26, now for רבינא's second version.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Fainting is not a real worry, so the line between established and non-established people does not hold.

steps.title: Why רבא does not explain like אביי
steps.stepSummary: רבא does not accept אביי's explanation because of the difficulty רבא himself raised against it from the case of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא did not say like אביי, because of his difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why רבא and אביי each reject the other's explanation, starting with רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא challenged אביי from the law of wine: a Jew going in and out is enough there. So רבא sees no reason to demand more for slaughter. That earlier challenge is what keeps רבא from accepting אביי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: His difficulty (the challenge he raised earlier)

phrases.english: רבא did not say like אביי,
because of his difficulty.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבא's own earlier challenge from the case of wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the summary, now turning to אביי and רבא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's earlier challenge from wine stops him from accepting אביי's explanation.

steps.title: Why אביי does not explain like רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבא's comparison to wine: there the non-Jew does not touch the wine, but here the כותי touches the animal while slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי did not say like רבא: there, he does not touch; here, he touches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives אביי's side: why the wine case does not prove anything about slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the wine case the non-Jew is not handling the wine, so a Jew coming in and out is enough. In שחיטה the כותי is actively handling the animal and could ruin the slaughter in a moment. So for אביי, going in and out is not enough here.

keyTerms.meaning: Touches (handles directly)
There (the wine case) / here (the slaughter case)

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא rejected the others for a specific reason: the wording 'וכולן', where the main source belongs, the רוב of experts, not worrying about fainting, and whether the outsider touches the item.

phrases.english: אביי did not say like רבא,
there, he does not touch,
phrases.notes: "There" is the wine case: the non-Jew is near the wine but not handling it.

phrases.english: here, he touches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other half of step 28: אביי's answer to רבא's wine comparison.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For אביי, slaughter differs from wine because the כותי touches the animal, so going in and out is not enough.

steps.title: Why רב אשי did not explain the משנה like אביי or רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי did not follow אביי or רבא, because he holds that כותים are גרי אריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי did not explain the משנה like either of them, because he holds that כותים are 'lion converts'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב אשי did not accept the explanations of אביי and רבא, who both explained the משנה as talking about a כותי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי holds that כותים converted only out of fear of the lions, so their conversion does not count. A כותי is then like a non-Jew, whose שחיטה is never valid. So the משנה cannot be talking about a כותי, and רב אשי had to explain it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Like both of them (here, אביי and רבא)
The people settled in ארץ ישראל who converted. Their Jewish status is questioned.
'Lion converts': they converted only out of fear of the lions that attacked them, so the conversion is not real
Because he holds

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רב אשי argues about how to slaughter. He argues about who a כותי is. If a כותי is not a Jew, his שחיטה is like a non-Jew's.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi did not say like both of them,
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means אביי and רבא, who both explained the משנה as talking about a כותי.

phrases.english: because he holds: Kutim are lion-converts.
phrases.notes: This points to the story in מלכים ב פרק יז, where lions attacked them until they took on the Jewish religion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth between אביי and רבא, the גמרא explains why רב אשי chose neither approach.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רב אשי, a כותי has the status of a non-Jew, so the משנה cannot be about a כותי.

steps.title: Why אביי did not explain the משנה like רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: אביי did not explain like רב אשי, because he does not accept רבא's ruling about a Jewish מומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי did not explain it like רב אשי, because he does not agree with what רבא said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי did not use רב אשי's explanation, which says the משנה is about a Jewish מומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's explanation depends on רבא's ruling: a Jew who eats נבלות to satisfy his appetite may slaughter if his knife is checked first. אביי does not accept that ruling. So he cannot explain the משנה that way.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold that view
A Jew who regularly sins in a certain area, here eating נבלות

phrases.english: Abaye did not say like Rav Ashi,
because he does not hold that of Rava.
phrases.notes: 'That of רבא' is רבא's ruling that a Jew who eats נבלות for his appetite may slaughter once his knife is checked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining each אמורא's choice. Now the גמרא turns to אביי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי rejects רבא's ruling about the מומר, so רב אשי's explanation is not open to him.

steps.title: Why didn't רבא follow his own ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא did not explain the משנה according to his own ruling, the way רב אשי did.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא, what is the reason he did not explain it according to his own teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רבא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does hold the ruling about the Jewish מומר. רב אשי's explanation is built on that ruling. So we would expect רבא to explain the משנה the same way as רב אשי, not as talking about a כותי.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
His own teaching or ruling

phrases.english: But Rava, what is the reason
that he did not say according to his own teaching?
phrases.notes: 'His own teaching' is the ruling about a Jewish מומר. רב אשי used that same ruling to explain the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רָבָא, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כִּשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רב אשי and אביי, the גמרא questions רבא's choice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבא explained the משנה as talking about a כותי when his own ruling would support רב אשי's explanation.

steps.title: רבא was only speaking according to אביי
steps.stepSummary: רבא's explanation about the כותי was said only within אביי's approach. It is not his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to אביי's words, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבא's explanation was only meant to work inside אביי's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא was answering אביי on אביי's own terms. He was saying: even if you explain the משנה as talking about a כותי, it should be explained my way. His own view is still the explanation based on his ruling about the מומר.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his words: arguing within someone else's approach

steps.whatToRemember: Each explanation fits its author. רב אשי treats כותים as non-Jews. אביי rejects רבא's ruling about the מומר. רבא spoke about a כותי only to fit אביי's approach.

phrases.english: He was speaking according to the words of Abaye,
but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא was only explaining within אביי's approach. He does not actually hold that explanation himself.

steps.title: A ברייתא on when a כותי's שחיטה is permitted
steps.stepSummary: A כותי's שחיטה is permitted when a Jew stands over him. If no Jew watched, the Jew gives him a כזית of the meat. If he eats it, the meat is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the slaughter of a כותי is permitted. When is that? When a Jew stands over him. But if the Jew came later and found he had already slaughtered, he cuts off a כזית and gives it to him. If he eats it, one may eat from his slaughter. If not, it is forbidden to eat from his slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives the rules for meat slaughtered by a כותי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a Jew watching, we know the שחיטה was done properly. Without one, we test the כותי by having him eat from the meat himself. If he eats it, he must consider it properly slaughtered, so we can trust his שחיטה. If he refuses, he knows something was wrong, so the meat is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? This limits a rule to a specific case.
Standing over him, watching him
An olive's volume, the standard amount for eating
Kosher slaughter of an animal

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא makes clear that a כותי's slaughter may be trusted, but only with a check: a Jew watching, or the eating test.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: the slaughter of a Kuti is permitted,
In what case are these words said?
When a Jew is standing over him,
but if he came and found that he had already slaughtered,
he cuts off an olive-bulk and gives it to him,
if he ate it, it is permitted to eat from his slaughter,
and if not, it is forbidden to eat from his slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of the different explanations, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about the שחיטה of a כותי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כותי's שחיטה is permitted when a Jew watches. If no Jew watched, the meat is permitted only if the כותי eats a כזית of it.

steps.title: A similar case: what the Jew finds in the Samaritan's possession
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא opens a parallel case in which a Jew finds something in a כותי's possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, if the Jew found in the possession of the כותי...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is setting up a new case that follows the same pattern as the כזית test it just taught. The case is not finished here; it continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ' (similarly) tells us the coming case is judged the same way as the previous one. In Step 34 we test the כותי by seeing whether he himself eats from his own שחיטה. The new case also starts with something the Jew finds in the כותי's hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly; a case that works the same way as the one just taught
He found
Literally 'in his hand'; in his possession

phrases.english: Similarly,
if the Jew found in the possession of the Samaritan

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from Step 34, adding a parallel case that follows the same logic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא begins a new case, about something the Jew finds in a כותי's possession, that is judged the same way as the case before it. The details continue in the next part of the text.
